title: Week in Orbit
summary: This week, the space industry is buzzing with new funding rounds, acquisitions, and a few notable technological developments. From optical ground stations to lunar defense preparations, the landscape is evolving, albeit with some hiccups in hypersonic testing.

themes.title: Funding for Ground Stations
themes.body: QOSMIC's recent $3.33 million raise highlights the growing interest in the orbital data economy. Optical ground stations are becoming a focal point as the demand for data from space increases.

themes.title: Acquisitions and Collaborations
themes.body: Voyager's acquisition of Astrobotic signals a consolidation trend in the lunar exploration sector. Meanwhile, Anduril and L3Harris teaming up for a tactical SDA constellation bid reflects a strategic push towards enhanced space situational awareness.

themes.title: Military Space Resilience Boost
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup's $1.4 billion allocation for space resilience indicates a serious commitment to fortifying U.S. capabilities in orbit. This funding could catalyze advancements in both defensive and offensive space technologies.

themes.title: Hypersonic Testing Delays
themes.body: The latest hypersonic glide-vehicle test has slipped yet again, marking the third consecutive quarter of delays. This raises questions about the reliability of hypersonic technologies amid increasing geopolitical tensions.
